question: Biopsy of a suspected juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA) is absolutely contraindicated in the outpatient clinic because the tumour is highly vascular and even a small biopsy can precipitate catastrophic, life-threatening haemorrhage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and represents one of the most important safety rules in ENT. JNA contains large, thin-walled vascular channels without smooth muscle. Even a small stab biopsy in the outpatient setting can trigger haemorrhage that cannot be controlled without surgical intervention. Diagnosis must be achieved by imaging alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. JNA is one of the most vascular tumours in ENT. Outpatient biopsy can cause immediate, uncontrollable, potentially fatal bleeding. Diagnosis is made on clinical grounds (adolescent male, recurrent severe epistaxis, progressive nasal obstruction) combined with CT and MRI. Biopsy is NEVER performed in the clinic — if tissue is ever needed, it is obtained only in the operating theatre with full anaesthetic cover, blood cross-matched, and embolisation capability on standby.
